note: Every row is a real, counted record with a real denominator — and NO TWO ROWS MEASURE THE SAME THING. That is deliberate, it is stated on the chart itself, and it is the argument of the act: put five different tests on one axis and you get a ranking that looks authoritative and means nothing. Percentages are hits divided by attempts, rounded.
source: Economists: An, Jalles & Loungani, IMF WP/18/39 (2018) — 5 of 153 recessions predicted by the consensus in the April before. Perma-bear base rate: 27 bear markets in the 96 years 1928–2024 (Ned Davis Research / Hartford Funds). Darts and professionals: the Wall Street Journal's Investment Dartboard contest, 142 contests between 1988 and 2002 — the professionals' picks beat the darts in 87 and beat the Dow itself in 76. Octopus Paul: Sea Life Centre Oberhausen — 4 of 6 at Euro 2008 and 8 of 8 at the 2010 World Cup.

oracles.name: Economists
oracles.measures: Recessions the forecasting consensus saw coming a year ahead, 1992–2014

oracles.name: A man with a sign
oracles.measures: Years that actually contained a 20% fall — i.e. the score for shouting "crash" every January and doing nothing else

oracles.name: A dartboard
oracles.measures: Rounds the Wall Street Journal's darts beat the professionals, 1988–2002

oracles.name: Stock pickers
oracles.measures: Rounds those professionals beat the Dow itself — a coin flip, with fees

oracles.name: Octopus Paul
oracles.measures: Football matches called correctly by walking into one of two boxes of mussels

paul.name: Paul
paul.method: Two boxes, each with a mussel and a flag. Whichever he opened first was the prediction.

tetlock.note: The line everyone quotes is "dart-throwing chimpanzee". Tetlock has said he never wrote it quite that way. What he did find: the average expert barely beat chance, and lost to a simple rule that just extrapolated the recent past.
